chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj and Hammad, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who employed a wet-nurse, so he handed over to her his son. So the wet-nurse went and handed over his son to another wet-nurse. So she disappeared with him for a while. Then the man sought his son from the wet-nurse whom he had given his son to. So she confessed that she had contracted it out, and confessed of the capture of his son, and that she had handed him over to another wet-nurse. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon her is the wergild (blood money), or she comes up with him'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wet-nurse subcontracts her care of a child to another nurse?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the wet-nurse (zay'ra) as a trustee (amin) in her contractual duty, illustrating the principle of 'sub-delegation without permission' (ta'wil) in Shia fiqh. The Imam's ruling that she must either return the child or pay diyah highlights the strict liability for loss or disappearance when the primary custodian fails to ensure direct care, a key concept in Islamic commercial law regarding amanah.
